items.title: A letter at the door
items.arabic: عِنْدَمَا فَتَحَ سَامِي بَابَ الْبَيْتِ، وَجَدَ رِسَالَةً عَلَى الْأَرْضِ. كَانَ اسْمُ أُخْتِهِ عَلَيْهَا، وَلَكِنَّهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ فِي الْبَيْتِ. وَضَعَ الرِّسَالَةَ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ لِيَشْتَرِيَ الْخُبْزَ. بَعْدَ نِصْفِ سَاعَةٍ عَادَ، فَلَمْ يَجِدِ الرِّسَالَةَ. سَمِعَ صَوْتَ أُخْتِهِ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ، فَسَأَلَهَا عَنْهَا. قَالَتْ: «نَعَمْ، قَرَأْتُهَا. إِنَّهَا مِنْ صَدِيقَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍ».

questions.prompt: Who was the letter addressed to?
Why did Sami leave the house?
What had happened to the letter when he returned?

items.structure: Follow the sequence: Sami finds the letter → leaves it on the table → goes out → returns. His sister is absent at first but is in the kitchen when he returns. In سَأَلَهَا عَنْهَا, the first ـها is his sister and the second is the letter.
items.english: When Sami opened the door, he found a letter on the floor. His sister’s name was on it, but she was not at home. He put it on the table and went out to buy bread. Half an hour later he returned and could not find the letter. He heard his sister in the kitchen and asked her about it. She said, “Yes, I read it. It is from an old friend.”

items.title: The house in the photograph
items.arabic: كَانَتْ مَرْيَمُ تَظُنُّ أَنَّ الْبَيْتَ الَّذِي تَرَكَتْهُ فِي طُفُولَتِهَا لَمْ يَعُدْ مَوْجُودًا. لِذَلِكَ دَهِشَتْ حِينَ رَأَتْ صُورَتَهُ فِي جَرِيدَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍ. لَمْ تَكُنِ الصُّورَةُ جَدِيدَةً، لَكِنَّ الْخَبَرَ الْمَكْتُوبَ تَحْتَهَا كَانَ يَقُولُ إِنَّ الْبَيْتَ سَيُصْبِحُ مَتْحَفًا. أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ إِلَيْهِ، لَا لِتَرَى الْغُرَفَ فَقَطْ، بَلْ لِتَعْرِفَ إِنْ كَانَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ الَّتِي زَرَعَهَا أَبُوهَا لَا تَزَالُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ.

questions.prompt: Before seeing the photograph, what did Maryam believe?
options: The house was already a museum
The house would become a museum
The photograph had been taken yesterday

questions.prompt: What particularly drew her back to the house?
options: She wanted to buy the newspaper
She wanted to see whether her father’s tree was still there
She wanted to replace the furniture

items.structure: لَمْ يَعُدْ مَوْجُودًا means “no longer existed.” The clause الَّذِي تَرَكَتْهُ فِي طُفُولَتِهَا describes the house. لَا ... فَقَطْ، بَلْ ... means “not only …, but …”. At the end, لَا تَزَالُ means “is still”; it is not a statement that the tree is absent.
items.english: Maryam thought the house she had left in childhood no longer existed. So she was surprised to see its photograph in an old newspaper. The photograph was not new, but the report beneath it said the house would become a museum. She wanted to go there, not only to see the rooms, but to find out whether the tree her father had planted was still in the garden.

limitations: Exploratory personal assessment, not a validated proficiency or clinical test.
Meaning-choice latency includes reading the choices and tapping; it is not pure lexical access time.
Timing excludes only marked interruptions, never responses simply because they were slow.
Different words appear in each form/vowel group. Differences are descriptive, not isolated causal effects.
Passage support follows first-pass answers. Later improvements include rereading and explanation.
The still-construction probe follows optional instruction in passage support; interpret it as possible near transfer.

timingMethod: Client performance.now from font-ready animation frame to response. Marked interruptions are excluded from timing summaries. No latency-based outlier deletion.
